exposure: parental co-exposure to metal mixture (25 metals)
cohort: The study cohort consisted of 1680 couples from the Jiangsu Birth Cohort (JBC) study, from whom urine samples were collected during the first trimester.
finding: Higher concentrations of maternal urinary cobalt and copper, and paternal and maternal urinary antimony, were significantly associated with an increased risk of preterm birth, with a positive joint effect observed for parental metal mixture concentrations.
